text:
Maya (People Ops): Heads up — a few folks asked about year-end 401(k) contribution cutoffs and how catch-up contributions (age 50+) get processed. Can payroll confirm the final submission date we should tell people?

Ethan: Is this for the Dec 31 payroll or the last payment that posts in the calendar year? Some vendors treat those differently.

Priya: Vendor (RetireCo) only allows allocations on the payroll run date — so if payroll sends on 12/30 for a 12/31 check, contributions go into the plan with the 12/31 date. The key is our payroll submission cutoff.

Maya (People Ops): Great. Can we publish a single line for the benefits site like: "Last payroll submission for 2026 plan-year contributions: 12/24 11:59pm PT" — does that sound right?

Payroll Bot: Submission window reminder: final 2026 off-cycle submission closes 2026-12-24 23:59 PT. Late files will be processed in January. :calendar:

Ethan: That 12/24 cutoff works operationally IF we get sign-off on dec 23 reconciliations. Anything after that risks being applied in Jan. Also note holiday bank closures can delay actual posting.

Ben (Finance): Confirming: if a catch-up (age 50+) election is added after the cutoff, we can do a manual adjustment only if the vendor accepts retro entries. RetireCo charges an administrative fee for post-close adjustments and sometimes rejects retro entries for the plan year. We should advise employees to submit changes earlier.

Priya: To be safe, we should provide two helpful notes on the benefits page: one for employees (what to aim for) and one for managers/payroll (internal guidance). Suggest copy: 
```
Employee note: To guarantee 2026 pretax or catch-up deferrals are taken in 2026, submit elections by 11:59pm PT on 2026-12-24. Changes after this date may not be recorded until the next payroll and could be non-reversible.
Payroll/Finance note: Final submission file for 2026 must be uploaded to RetireCo by 2026-12-24 23:59 PT. Reconciliations completed by 2026-12-23 preferred. Retro manual adjustments may incur fees and are subject to vendor acceptance.
```

Maya (People Ops): Perfect — Priya, Ben: can you confirm by end of day so I can publish? Also, does this affect HSA pre-tax treatment for last pay? A few folks asked if FSA/HSA deductions stop when they leave mid-December.

Ben (Finance): HSA deductions follow payroll elections. If a person terminates before the payroll cutoff and we process final payroll, deductions stop. If termination happens after cutoff and payroll was submitted, vendor posts as usual and then final check might show adjustments. For FSA, dependent on plan rules — run specifics with BenefitsVendor.

Priya: I'll ping RetireCo and BenefitsVendor now and ask about retro acceptance window + FSA termination interplay. Will report back with a clear FAQ blurb.

Ethan: One more ops flag — for employees turning 50 in December: catch-up eligibility is based on age on 12/31 of the calendar year. So if they turn 50 on 12/30, they're eligible for the whole calendar year. Make sure the employee-facing copy says that.

Maya (People Ops): Excellent catch. Final checklist before we post: 1) Confirm vendor retro policy (Priya) 2) Confirm payroll cut/freeze times and publish timezone (Ethan) 3) Finance note on fees/refunds (Ben) 4) Add age/eligibility line for catch-up (Maya). Please reply here when done. :white_check_mark:

Priya: On it — will update by EOD.

Ben (Finance): Will confirm fees and a short sentence for the page by EOD.

Payroll Bot: Reminder scheduled: benefits site update draft due 2026-12-01.
